§7.1 Text Formatting Conventions

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-text-formatting-conventions · text formatting inline

✅ Normative

Inline marks MUST be written with exactly the markup in the table below. Where Markdown has no syntax for a mark, the output MUST use the HTML element named here and MUST NOT use a notation of its own.

This is the inline-markup table for the whole protocol. Each row states its requirement; the linked rule holds the detail, the sub-cases and the examples.

Printed mark Requirement Rule
Maths, inline or displayed MUST be LaTeX inside $$ … $$; single $ delimiters MUST NOT be used Inline Equations§7.2.6, Displayed Equations§7.2.2
Hyperlink or email address MUST be raw text by default; link syntax MAY be used only when link extraction was requested Links§7.2.8
Bold / italic MUST be Markdown **bold** / *italic*, and only where the glyphs are heavier or slanted Bold and Italics§7.2.1
Underline MUST be <u>…</u> Underlined Text§7.2.12
Strikeout MUST be ~~…~~ over exactly the struck glyphs Struck and Replaced Values§9.6.7
Superscript / subscript MUST be <sup>…</sup> / <sub>…</sub>, never a Unicode raised or lowered glyph Superscript and Subscript§7.2.11
Highlight MUST be <mark>…</mark> over exactly the highlighted run Highlighted Text§7.2.5
Highlight colour MUST be carried as style="background-color: HTML_COLOR_NAME" on the <mark>, using the nearest HTML colour name Highlighted Text§7.2.5, Text Colors§7.3.12
Text colour, when it is the only distinguisher MUST be <font color="HTML_COLOR_NAME">…</font> Text Colors§7.3.12
Signature MUST be [signature:{name}], or bare [signature] when the name is not legible Signatures§7.3.10
Logo MUST be [logo: printed words], or bare [logo] when it prints no text Logos§12.1.3
Watermark MUST be [watermark: printed words], first in its page's content Watermarks§7.3.13
Stamp MUST be [stamp: printed words], or bare [stamp] when illegible Stamps§7.3.11
A printed character that is also Markdown syntax MUST be escaped — \*\*, \_, \|, \` — and MUST NOT be dropped to avoid the collision Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4

Why HTML elements at all

Markdown has no syntax for underline, superscript, subscript or highlight. The HTML element passes through every downstream Markdown renderer unchanged, and it survives a round-trip: a reader can strip it, render it or read the base characters underneath. A Unicode substitute (², ₂) does not, which is why Superscript and Subscript§7.2.11 forbids it.
